obernants.approximation_semantics: Exact byte-level separator state before the first append; validation of every row precedes the single normalizing byte.
obernants.assumptions: Partial file readable as UTF-8; rows validated by the existing envelope checks; append and sync_data succeed.
obernants.domain: Supplied or worker-written codex-results.partial.jsonl bytes B: absent, empty, whitespace-only (space/tab/CR), rows with/without a final LF, rows followed by a whitespace tail or a bare CR.
obernants.evidence: Baseline red on 02f3d093 (merged line, trailing characters at column 265); the first predicate (last byte != LF) created a blank physical line for whitespace tails, red for a strict no-trim reader on 46e3ee9 (EOF while parsing a value); green after the tail predicate in debug and release.
obernants.observation_scope: Whether B ends with LF, and the exact bytes written before any ask.
obernants.operator: Let tail(B) be the segment after the last LF (all of B if none). sep(B) = tail(B).trim() is nonempty, i.e. a real record lacks its terminator. The worker writes exactly one LF iff sep(B), after all rows validate and before any ask; a whitespace-only tail is left in place and the next row is appended after it; an invalid row stops before that byte.

obernants.approximation_semantics: Byte-level composition of the published file as concatenation of retained prior bytes, optional LF and new rows.
obernants.assumptions: Single worker, successful asks and writes, rename succeeds; no hostile concurrent writer.
obernants.domain: Accepted partial bytes B and the remaining request sequence R in request order.
obernants.evidence: Tests assert starts_with(prior bytes), final LF, parsable rows and id order on five shapes; failed-next-request leaves B ++ LF exactly.
obernants.observation_scope: Exact final bytes and parsed row sequence.
obernants.operator: final = B ++ (LF if sep(B)) ++ concat(row(r) ++ LF for r in R); rows(.) is the nonblank trim-filtered parsed-row projection used by the worker and annot parse_results, not a physical line count; rows(final) = rows(B) ++ R; the original bytes are a prefix of the final file; a whitespace-only tail of B becomes leading whitespace of the first new row, so no blank physical line is introduced.

obernants.approximation_semantics: Fibers of the failure boundary at the partial file: which inputs stop before any byte is written and which leave a separated file.
obernants.assumptions: Existing envelope checks and sticky-error recording unchanged.
obernants.domain: Partial files with a truncated or invalid last row, unknown id, wrong model, duplicate id; and a failing next request after a repaired boundary.
obernants.evidence: Truncated last row: error contains incomplete, zero asks, bytes unchanged. FAIL after prior [a] without LF: one ask, partial equals prior ++ LF, sticky error, clean resume with three rows.
obernants.observation_scope: Partial-file bytes, source-level ask count (fake-process calls) and error sentinel after a failing run; other directory files are outside this fiber.
obernants.operator: Scoped to the partial file: invalid row -> no write to it, no ask, error (batch-id.txt, requests snapshot, lock/pid and codex-error.txt may still be written by run/execute/finish); valid rows and failing ask k -> partial bytes B ++ (LF if sep(B)) ++ rows of successes before k, sticky error; resume never repeats rows(B), rows(.) being the nonblank parsed-row projection, not physical lines. A bare CR after a complete last row is trailing JSON whitespace: the row is accepted and sep is true, so CR files are not rejected.
